title: MX products at three payload formats, two paths, nonuniform scales
surface: matmul_mx(dst, a, b, scale_a, scale_b, m=, n=, k=) against l1_to_l0_mx + mmad_mx; gm_to_l1_mx_scale_nd2nz packing dense scale codes; Tensor.reinterpret to DT.fp4_e2m1 / DT.fp4_e1m2 / DT.e4m3 / DT.e5m2; the DT.mx_e4m3 and DT.mx_e5m2 compatibility aliases
study_for: The aliases do not attach scales. `DT.mx_e4m3` and `DT.mx_e5m2` name the same physical bytes as the ordinary FP8 storage types; what makes a product an MX product is the `l1_to_l0_mx` load and the `mmad_mx` / `matmul_mx` compute. Reading the alias as 'the MX type' is the misunderstanding this example is arranged to prevent -- and the alias form needs the M10-017 repair, while the reference is unchanged either way.

Two paths over one set of inputs. The shortcut is one call; the explicit path allocates L0A and L0B tensors, loads each operand with its scale through `l1_to_l0_mx`, and computes with `mmad_mx`. Every format runs both, and the pair agreeing is what establishes that the shortcut is the same operation rather than a similar one.

The scales are dense per row and per K32 group, and nonuniform in both directions on purpose -- `125 + (row + group) % 5` for one operand and a different combination for the other. A packing that transposed the two axes, or a compute that took group 0's scale for every group, produces a power-of-two error in a whole row or a whole 32-column band, which the failure output points at.

The reference decodes the payloads without the library. FP8 is arithmetic -- exponent field, fraction, bias, and the subnormal branch -- and FP4 is a lookup table per layout, with A as E2M1 and B as E1M2 in the mixed case. No ascriptor codec is imported, so the decode is genuinely independent of the thing being checked.

Why it can be bitwise. The payload pools are restricted exponent bands and the scale codes are 125..129, so every value is dyadic and the whole 128-element dot product lands exactly in FP32. Widen either and the comparison has to become a tolerance -- and then it stops being able to see a one-group scale error.
do_not_copy_when: You need a transposed or compact-tail MX tile. This example declares a fully aligned, untransposed K=128 tile and establishes nothing else: no transpose, no compact tail, no exceptional scale codes, and no FP8 mixed with FP4 in one product.
Your payloads span the whole format. The exponent bands here are chosen so the dot product is exact; arbitrary FP8 values need a tolerance and a different argument about what the comparison proves.

You expected the dtype to carry the scale. It does not. A kernel that loads an MX operand with an ordinary `l1_to_l0` and then calls `mmad_mx` has no scales attached, and nothing in the type system will say so.
